name: Het Scheepvaartmuseum
description: ’s Lands Zeemagazijn was built in 1656 by Daniel Stalpaert on the new island of Kattenburg as the naval arsenal of the Amsterdam Admiralty: a square, four-winged block of pale stone round a courtyard, where rigging, sails, cannon and provisions for the fleet were stored, with a pedimented pavilion in the middle of each side. Since 1973 it has housed the national maritime museum, and in 2011 the courtyard got a glass roof. A full-size replica of the VOC ship Amsterdam lies at the quay outside.
funFact: The pediment on the water side shows Neptune and the Admiralty arms; the doors and tall arched openings once let cannon and masts in from the quay, which is why the ground floor is raised and arched while the upper floors have plain sash windows.
